title: Yearly time shifts gave no clear three-day antipodal earthquake count excess after 114 M7+ events in 2017-2025
abstract: We tested a reported remote earthquake count increase in a later period. A fixed ComCat snapshot gave 26 M5.5+ pairs in the three days after 114 M7+ sources in 2017-2025, and 35 pairs before. Targets were within 30 degrees of the antipode. The difference was -9 and the after-to-before ratio was 0.743. A reference with 99,999 common target-time shifts within each year gave a one-sided p value of 0.80641 for an increase. Its central 95% count-difference range was -25 to 29. The 2000-2016 comparison gave 112 pairs after and 50 before, with p = 0.00686. The year 2010 supplied 43 of the 62 excess pairs. After removal of that year, an exploratory check gave p = 0.12424. All four planned later-period cap and window checks had nonpositive differences. These tests give no clear later count excess. They do not rule out remote triggering, establish physical suppression, or prove a change between periods. Short records, target clusters, mixed magnitude methods and yearly phase assumptions limit inference. Code, aggregate evidence, source hashes, figures and separate count checks are included. External event records stay outside the package.
